text:
Teuvo Teravainen, a Stanley Cup winner with Chicago in 2015, is 32 now and playing under 15 minutes a night, with 6 points in 15 games, close to the pace he set last season (35 points in 75 games). The trouble is the last ten: one assist, where we'd expect about 5 points at his ice time.

Our numbers split that dip. Chicago is getting fewer chances than usual with him on the ice, and the ones it gets haven't gone in: the team has scored 3.0 fewer goals than its chances deserve with him out there. At five on five the Blackhawks get only 41% of the expected goals (the share of chance quality) with him on. Evolving-Hockey noted last season that he played with some of the weakest teammates in the league, so not all of that is on him.

What he isn't doing is shooting: 11 shots in 15 games, and his individual expected goals are down to 0.29 per 60 from 0.50. His ice time is up 1:48 a night over the last ten games; we'd watch whether that brings more pucks on net.
headline: Teuvo Teravainen, quiet in a rough Chicago stretch
